reading.title: Feelings Come in Layers
reading.purpose: Learn precise words for feelings that look ahead, look back, or pull in two directions.
paras: Feelings are not always simple. Sometimes you feel two things at once, such as on the last day of elementary school, which can feel bittersweet, both happy and sad together. Learning exact words for feelings helps you understand yourself and tell others what you mean.

Some feelings look ahead. Anticipation is the excitement of waiting for something good, like a birthday trip. Dread is a strong fear about what may happen, such as before a hard test. When news is worse than you expected, you may feel dismay, a sudden shock and worry.

Other feelings look back. Regret is a sad feeling about something you did or did not do, like words you wish you could take back. Resentment is bitter anger about being treated unfairly, and it can grow if you hold on to it for a long time.

Some feelings are about wanting. Longing is a deep wish for something or someone you do not have, and to yearn is to want something very much, especially something far away or lost. A student who has moved to a new town might yearn for old friends.

Not every feeling is hard. Contentment is the quiet feeling of being satisfied with what you have. When a difficult moment comes, composure helps you stay calm and in control of your feelings. Naming a feeling is the first step toward handling it well.

choices: the excitement of waiting for something good to happen
a sudden shock at news that is worse than expected
bitter anger about being treated in an unfair way
strong fear about what may happen
qs.why: The text defines it: dread is "a strong fear about what may happen."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what it means to yearn?
choices: A student who has moved to a new town might yearn for old friends.
Longing is a deep wish for something or someone you do not have, and to yearn is to want something very much, especially something far away or lost.
Regret is a sad feeling about something you did or did not do, like words you wish you could take back.
qs.why: This sentence defines yearn: to want something very much, especially something far away or lost.

ev.text: Longing is a deep wish for something or someone you do not have, and to yearn is to want something very much, especially something far away or lost.

qs.q: Why might a student who has moved yearn for old friends?
choices: Old friends are far away, so the student misses them.
The student has been asked to forgive an old friend at school.
The student is waiting for a surprise birthday trip soon.
The student feels calm and content in the new town now.
qs.why: Yearning is wanting something far away or lost, and old friends in a different town fit that meaning.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Hard feelings always go away if a person ignores them.
Happy and sad feelings can never happen at the same time.
Exact words help people talk about feelings.
Only adults can feel regret, dread, or resentment.
qs.why: The reading gives exact words for many feelings and ends by saying that naming a feeling helps you handle it.
